description: Per-module benchmark record for the declared critical read paths, and the baseline the regression gate ratchets against. Produced by test/perf/measure-benchmark-manifest.mjs.
honesty: Every millisecond figure here is a LOWER BOUND. They are taken over loopback Postgres on a shared developer laptop, so they exclude pool wait, network round trip, serialization and every layer of the Nest request path. Buffer blocks and row counts are the numbers that ratchet; the milliseconds are recorded because the ceiling is stated in milliseconds, not because they estimate production.

requestCeilingsMs.note: Request-level ceilings ARE measured, by test/perf/route-budget-http.seeded-e2e-spec.ts, and recorded under `requestLevel`. The cache-hit ceiling remains unmeasured — no Redis runs against this seed.

subject.what: A content digest of every file whose SQL this manifest measures, taken as it was read. A release SHA cannot detect an uncommitted edit to another ticket's catalog; this can.
subject.note: MEASURED AGAINST AN UNCOMMITTED CATALOG: contracts/route-budgets.json. The numbers describe the working tree, not the release SHA, and are reproducible only from that tree.

machine.note: A shared developer laptop running other agents concurrently. Load average is recorded because it is the single largest source of wall-clock variance in these numbers.

container.detail: win32 — no cgroup; the process is not container-limited

database.name: scratch_local
database.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 on x86_64-windows, compiled by msvc-19.44.35228, 64-bit
database.transport: loopback TCP (127.0.0.1) — no network round trip, no pool proxy

instruments: src/scripts/run-read-cost-budgets.mjs — EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS), percentiles over N samples
test/perf/measure-heavy-query-plans.mjs — cold/warm buffers plus retained plan text
test/perf/benchmark-environment.mjs — dataset size, machine limits, concurrency and error rate
method.tenantSkew: The same statement picks different plans per tenant on this seed, so every benchmark is recorded against all four rather than the majority tenant alone.
method.datasetAttribution: A module's dataset counts the tables the MODULE owns. A read that joins another module's table is still measured in full, but those rows are counted under the module that owns them — dashboard-home owns only `announcements`, and its section reads are measured over the notifications, calendar, build and attendance datasets recorded under those modules.
method.replicateOrdering: Replicates are ordered large -> mid -> small -> tiny -> large again, so a tenant's own replicates are separated by three other tenants' work. Consecutive reruns of one tenant would measure a cache that never moves, understate variance, and calibrate the gate too tight — which is the direction that produces false alarms.

noiseStudy.what: The same measurement repeated against unchanged code. The regression thresholds below are derived from this, not chosen.
noiseStudy.stabilityNote: Relative replicate-to-replicate swing of each metric on UNCHANGED code, across every benchmark and tenant. This table is the whole argument for what the gate ratchets on: a metric whose worst swing is 0 can be ratcheted exactly, and one whose worst swing is larger than any regression worth catching cannot be ratcheted at all.

falsePositives.what: Every replicate of UNCHANGED code, on every tenant, replayed against replicate 1 through the real gate. Anything above zero is a gate that will be muted within a week.

timing.disarmedBecause: unchanged code moved by up to 234% (4.745 ms absolute) between replicates on this harness — above the 25% relative AND 1 ms absolute arming thresholds. A gate with a noise floor that wide cannot distinguish a regression from a rerun, so timing is recorded and reported but does not decide the exit code. Buffers, rows, plan shape and statement counts do.

regressionPolicy.deterministicIsGlobalFallback: policy.deterministic is derived from the WORST swing across every benchmark and is only used where a per-benchmark stability record is missing. The gate prefers each benchmark's own envelope, because one unstable benchmark must not widen the band for the rest.
regressionPolicy.provenance: derived from 3 replicates of unchanged code: worst deterministic swing 9919 absolute / 19000.0%, worst timing swing 234.4%

notMeasured: Request-level figures cover 188 of 204 route×tenant slots (n=2 replicates, 376 measurements total) on scratch_local; 32 were declined and 0 failed. See requestLevel.tally.refusalsByReason for why each was not measured.
Cache-hit latency. No Redis is running against this seed, so every number here is the cache-MISS path.
